summary: Vienna-born, New York-raised Edward Bernays built modern public relations, using paid experts and staged events to sell cigarettes to women despite cancer warnings, and propaganda that helped bring about the 1954 coup in Guatemala.

evidence.note: born in Vienna in 1891 to a family related to Freud
family moves to New York City when he is one
first publicity campaign for the play Damaged Goods, around 1913
long segment on wife and partner Doris Fleischman and her uncredited work
hired by American Tobacco to get women smoking Lucky Strikes
1933 memo urges client to prepare a counter-offensive against cancer findings
commissions a doctor's claim that bacon is a healthy breakfast
image work for Coolidge and campaign strategy for Hoover against FDR
United Fruit's grip on Guatemala and Bernays's campaign for it
CIA-backed coup of June 1954 ousts Arbenz
death in March 1995; the host gives his age as 104

notes: Host says Bernays died at 104; he was 103 (1891-1995). The later Guatemalan civil war and genocide get a few minutes as consequences of the coup; genocide-mass-killing left out as not a long enough segment. WWI propaganda (Committee on Public Information era) folded into the primary theme. Modern PR-vs-journalism legacy is a short coda, so reaches_present is false.
